title: Price accepts Infinity and huge values; JSON.stringify then sends null as the price
evidence: Number("Infinity") and Number("1e999") are Infinity, and Infinity > 0 is true, so the line is accepted. validQuantity (guards.js:16) also accepts a 400-digit string, because Number(qty) is Infinity and Infinity >= 1. The total then shows "Infinity", and JSON.stringify(lines) at line 26 writes Infinity as null.
failing_case: Enter client A, quantity 1, price 1e999, click Add line, then Send invoice. The page shows Total: Infinity. The POST body is [{"client":"A","qty":1,"price":null}]. The server receives a billing line with no price.
remediation: Validate with Number.isFinite, set an upper bound on price and quantity, and parse the price to integer minor units (cents) in one named function.

title: Send is guarded by a 1-second timer, not by an in-flight flag, and success changes nothing the user can see, so a second invoice is easy to send
evidence: app.js:25-29 and guards.js:19-26. The only duplicate guard is tooSoon(), which compares Date.now() to the last click. After a 2xx the handler only does sentCount += 1; sentCount is read nowhere. The lines array is not cleared, the button is not disabled and no message is shown.
failing_case: Add one line, click Send invoice. The server takes 3 s. The page shows nothing. After 1.5 s the user clicks again, tooSoon() returns false, and a second POST of the same lines is sent. Even after a fast success the list and total still show the invoice, so the user clicks Send again and a duplicate invoice is created. No invoice id or idempotency key is sent, so the server cannot detect it.
remediation: Disable the button while the request is pending (in-flight flag in a finally), send an idempotency key per invoice, and on success show a confirmation, clear the lines and show the invoice reference.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: A network failure on Send is never caught, so the user gets no message
evidence: app.js:24-29. Only a non-ok response is handled (line 27). fetch() rejects on offline, DNS failure, or a dropped connection. The async click handler has no try/catch, so the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and the alert on line 27 never runs.
failing_case: Go offline, add a line, click Send invoice. fetch rejects with TypeError. Nothing is shown; the console logs an unhandled rejection. The user cannot tell whether the invoice went out. A second click within 1 s is also silently swallowed by tooSoon().
remediation: Wrap the fetch in try/catch and show the same failure message with a retry action; apply the same to the void request.

title: The invoice being built lives only in memory and lines cannot be edited or removed
evidence: app.js:1, 20. Lines are only ever pushed. There is no remove or edit control (index.html:21 is a plain list), no localStorage, and no beforeunload warning.
failing_case: Enter 12 lines, then notice line 4 has the wrong price. There is no way to fix it; the only option is to reload, which discards all 12 lines. An accidental refresh or tab close also loses everything.
remediation: Add per-line Remove and Edit buttons, and persist a draft (versioned, guarded parse) or warn on unload.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is summed as unrounded floats while lines display rounded prices; the total can disagree with the visible lines
evidence: Traced app.js:5-12. Each row shows l.price.toFixed(2) but the total uses the raw float price. Price is accepted with any number of decimals (app.js:19 only checks > 0). The pricing arithmetic lives in the render function, not in a named, tested function. Not executed: Bash was unavailable to this reviewer.
failing_case: Enter qty 3, price 1.005. The row shows '3 × 1.00' (1.005.toFixed(2) is '1.00') while the total is 3.015 and shows as 3.01 or 3.02, never 3.00. Price 0.004 is accepted and shows '1 × 0.00', yet is posted as 0.004. The invoice total disagrees with its lines.
remediation: Store prices as integer minor units, reject more than two decimals at input, and move line and total arithmetic to one pure function with a test. Render only its result.

title: A whitespace-only client name passes the required check and is stored as an empty string
evidence: index.html:14 uses the native required attribute, which accepts "   ". app.js:16 trims it to "" and nothing checks the result before the push on line 20.
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, quantity 2, price 5, press Add line. The line is added with client ""; it renders as an empty link followed by ': 2 × 5.00' and is sent to the server.
remediation: Check the trimmed value is not empty and show a field error.

title: Send posts an empty invoice when no lines have been added
evidence: app.js:24-26. There is no check on lines.length before the POST. The page opens with lines = [] and the Send button enabled (index.html:23).
failing_case: Open the page and click Send invoice immediately. POST /api/invoices is sent with body "[]". If the server accepts it, a blank invoice is created and the page gives no feedback.
remediation: Disable Send until at least one line exists, and re-check in the handler.

title: A successful send shows nothing and leaves the lines in place, inviting a duplicate
evidence: sentCount is written here and read nowhere. The response body is never read, lines is not cleared, no button state or text changes. The Void handler at app.js:34 also has no success path.
failing_case: User clicks Send. The request succeeds. The page looks identical to before, with the same lines and the Send button still live. User cannot tell it worked, clicks Send again after a second, and a duplicate invoice is created.
remediation: On success, show a status message such as 'Invoice sent' in an aria-live region, show the invoice id from the response, and clear or lock the lines. Remove sentCount or display it.

title: Void invoice is a dead button for the signed-in user: a silent return, with no disabled state and no reason
evidence: app.js:2 sets the user's roles to viewer and billing; guards.js:10-12 requires 'admin'. The button at index.html:24 is always rendered enabled (traced).
failing_case: Sam clicks Void invoice. canVoid returns false, the handler returns, and nothing happens. There is no 'You need the admin role', and no disabled or hidden button.
remediation: Hide or disable the button (with aria-disabled and the reason in text) for users without the role, and show a message if the action is refused.

title: Void names no invoice, asks for no confirmation, and reports no success
evidence: The POST has no body and no id; Send (line 26) never stores the id the server returns. index.html:23-24 puts Send and Void next to each other with identical styling (styles.css:4). Nothing is shown on a successful void (traced).
failing_case: An admin who has built a new draft clicks Void invoice by mistake next to Send. A request goes out that cannot say which invoice, so the server either rejects it or voids the latest one. There is no confirm, and a success looks the same as nothing happening.
remediation: Keep the id from the send response, post it in the void request, ask for confirmation naming the invoice, and show 'Invoice N voided'. Separate and style Void as a destructive secondary action.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently; Add line appears dead
evidence: Traced app.js:14-22. The submit handler returns with no message, no focus move and no aria-live text. index.html:16 and :18 have no required attribute, so the browser shows no native message either.
failing_case: User types Client 'Acme Ltd', Quantity '1.5' (or '2 pcs'), Price '9,50' and presses Add line. Nothing is added and nothing is said. The user cannot tell whether the click registered or which field is wrong (WCAG 3.3.1).
remediation: On failure, set an inline error next to the offending field (aria-describedby plus aria-invalid) saying what is wrong and what is accepted, and move focus to the first bad field. Also mark qty and price required in the HTML.

quote: const user = { name: "sam", roles: ["viewer", "billing"] };  // the signed-in user
title: The void permission is decided only in the browser, from a role list that is a client-side constant
evidence: guards.js:10-12 canVoid checks user.roles for "admin". The user object is a hardcoded, mutable global in app.js. The void request at app.js:33 carries no credential or role. No server-side check is in this payload.
failing_case: In the dev console run user.roles.push('admin'), then click Void invoice. The client check passes and POST /api/invoices/void is sent. Whether it is refused depends entirely on server code outside this change.
remediation: Treat canVoid as display logic only; enforce the admin check on the server for /api/invoices/void and fetch the user's roles from the session.

title: Each client name is rendered as a link to '#' that goes nowhere
evidence: app.js:8. The anchor has no destination. The title repeats the visible text.
failing_case: Tab through the page: each line adds a tab stop announced as a link. Activating one changes the URL to '#' and scrolls to the top, which moves the user away from the form.
remediation: Render the name as plain text, or link to a real client page; drop the redundant title.

title: The whole list is re-written on each add, so a screen reader re-announces every line
evidence: app.js:7 replaces the full innerHTML on each render, so every li is a new node in a live region. Validation errors, send results and void results are not in any live region.
failing_case: With 10 lines present, adding the 11th makes the screen reader read all 11 rows again. The messages that matter (errors, 'sent') are never announced.
remediation: Make the list a normal list, and announce through a separate polite status element with one short sentence per event, such as 'Line added, total 25.00'.
